title: General Construction of Time-Dependent Integrable Chiral Field Theories
abstract: We develop a general procedure for constructing time-dependent integrable chiral field theories from autonomous unitary difference-form $S$-matrices satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation. Spectral parameters are transported along the free right- and left-moving characteristics, defining a map from physical spacetime to spectral space on which the two-body scattering data are evaluated. Requiring spatially homogeneous right-left scattering forces the characteristic map to be affine. The inverse Cayley transform then determines the local contact interaction, while evaluation along the affine spectral trajectory fixes its time dependence. Thus, the nonautonomous interaction is determined by the autonomous scattering data together with chiral kinematics and spatial homogeneity, rather than being introduced independently. The Yang--Baxter equation supplies the factorized many-body transport, and on a spatial circle periodicity leads to quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (qKZ) equations whose compatibility defines a flat discrete transport in spectral space. Pulling the corresponding spectral-space amplitudes back to physical coordinates gives the time-dependent many-body wavefunctions. Rational $SU(N)$, trigonometric $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$, and rational $O(N)$ scattering illustrate how the same mechanism generates distinct nonautonomous interactions. The resulting framework gives a geometric route from autonomous factorized scattering data to time-dependent integrable field theories.
summary: This paper presents a general geometric construction for time-dependent integrable chiral field theories. It shows that the time evolution of the system's interaction is not arbitrary but is rigidly fixed by the initial autonomous scattering data and the constraints of chiral kinematics and spatial homogeneity. This provides a powerful, unified method for generating complex, nonautonomous integrable models.
main_problem: The paper develops a general mathematical procedure to construct time-dependent integrable chiral field theories starting only from autonomous unitary difference-form S-matrices satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation.
main_result: The nonautonomous dynamics are entirely determined by the initial autonomous scattering data, chiral kinematics, and the constraint of spatial homogeneity, providing a geometric route to time-dependent integrable systems.
method: The method involves mapping spectral parameters along free chiral characteristics to define a spectral space, using the inverse Cayley transform to derive the local interaction, and imposing spatial homogeneity to fix the time dependence.
model_or_system: The focus is on chiral field theories with linear dispersion, characterized by a Hamiltonian derived from a local contact interaction $V(u)$. The theory is analyzed using factorized scattering data derived from the S-matrix $S(u)$.
key_observables: The time-dependent Hamiltonian $H(t)$ and the resulting many-body wavefunctions.
important_parameters: The spectral parameter $u$, which evolves affinely in time as $u(t) = 2\kappa t +  eta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes chiral field theories with linear dispersion and requires spatial homogeneity of the right-left scattering forces.
paper_structure: The paper builds the framework by first establishing the connection between autonomous scattering data and the local interaction via the Cayley transform. It then uses chiral kinematics and spatial homogeneity to determine the time dependence of the interaction, leading to the final construction of the time-dependent Hamiltonian and wavefunctions.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting autonomous scattering data (a common input in integrable models) to time-dependent dynamics is highly relevant for understanding how external time-varying fields or time-dependent couplings affect integrable quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Characteristic map from physical spacetime to spectral space. Each spacetime event (x, t) determines the pair of spectral coordinates (ζR, ζL) associated with the right- and left-moving characteristics passing through that event. The colored curves in ZRL are the images of constant-time slices Mti under the characteristic map ι. They are equivalently level sets of the spectral difference uLR(ζR, ζL) = ζL −ζR. The pullback ι∗uLR = uLR ◦ι gives the spectral coordinate sampled by the right-left scattering process.
